newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks erase early losses to close firmer.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks erase early losses to close firmer.

text.p: Toronto's stock market reversed earlier losses to end on a firmer note on Friday, helped by stronger bonds after investors decided the key index had sold off enough in recent sessions.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index closed 11.79 points higher at 6382.12, aided by a rally in North American bond markets, said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investing.
The index dropped more than 50 points at the open after investors were spooked by a forecast of disappointing second quarter results from U.S. computer chip maker Intel Corp.

However, Toronto turned around as bonds rallied on signs of subdued inflation from Friday's U.S. economic data and moderate gains in the Canadian currency. Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose 1.00 to close at 112.10 for a yield of 7.027 percent.
"A very, very impressive reversal," Best said. "There had been a couple days' sell-off and there had been fill-in" as investors returned to snap up issues.
Turnover was active at 92 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
Canada's largest equities market lost ground for most of the week after setting record highs on Monday. Weekly losses totaled 57 points from Monday's open of 6441 points.
Investors are eyeing Monday's federal election in Canada, however a Liberal Party majority seemed almost assured according to recent polls, Best said.
It also looks like the two most right-wing parties, the Reform Party and Progressive Conservatives, will be in a race for Opposition seats.

Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-groups closed in positive territory, led by media, conglomerates, consumer products and banks. The weaker side included golds, utilities, forestry products and industrial products.
Advancing issues outpaced decliners 550 to 438 while 286 ended steady.
Among hot stocks telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly traded firm, slipped 0.30 to 36.35.
Heavyweight BCE topped most actives and pulled the rest of the market south.
Transportation firm Bombardier Inc. rose 0.25 to 29.00 after Friday's news that U.S.-based Comair Inc. signed a firm order for 18 aircraft worth $330 million.
